hints: Let dp[i] be the cheapest cost ending by killing monster i.
Each earlier kill contributes a line with slope equal to its new factor.
Use a Li Chao tree because strengths and factors need not be ordered.
analogy: Each possible last skill offers a cost line; query the lowest line at the current strength.
example: With initial factor 10, strengths [2,3], and factors [1,1], killing both costs 23 while killing only the final monster costs 30.
algorithm: Insert the initial line y=x_initial*t into a minimum Li Chao tree over strengths 1 through 10^6. For each i, query at s[i] to get dp[i], then insert y=f[i]*t+dp[i]. Print dp[n], using wide integer arithmetic.
correctness: The last kill before i determines both the previous minimum cost and the factor used at i. Its line evaluates to that transition, and querying all prior lines finds the exact minimum.
complexity: For n levels and coordinate domain X=10^6, O(n log X) time and O(X) space with a fixed tree.
